Resolves #19764
Related: neomjs/neo-agent-institution#674
Related: neomjs/neo-agent-institution#12

Native drag lookup now checks each resolver's own source window against the existing Window registry before calling it. A closed popup's retained target cannot invoke its retired native owner during another window's position event. A live main-window resolver can still name a separate popup, and renewed eligibility is read from the registry without a second cache.

Evidence: L3 (headed native-browser positive journey plus deterministic red/green regression) → L3 required (the bounded source-eligibility outcome). Residual: packaged Fleet replay, Residual-Owner: neomjs/neo-agent-institution#674.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered: the new `DragCoordinator.spec.mjs` arm disconnects the source through Window's real handler and checks both lookup and a later primary-window position event without invoking the retired resolver. |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: live main-to-popup control in the new arm and existing native-drag tests. Outside CI: the unchanged headed Workstation native-titlebar journey passes. |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: re-registering the source window makes its resolver eligible again; the zone itself was retained throughout. |
| AC-4 | Outside-CI red: the new arm fails on the base with `disconnected source resolver invoked`. The repaired coordinator suite passes; shared source gates also pass. |
| AC-5 | The [native finding and independent contract read](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19764#issuecomment-6197703848) distinguish this exception from the still-unclassified missing-parent delta observation retained on Institution's acceptance lane. |

## Deltas from ticket

No substantive behavior expansion. The existing SortZone cancellation fixture now includes its live originating source window; its candidate and cancellation assertions are unchanged. CI exposed that missing precondition after the coordinator suite passed. No NativeLifecycle error suppression, document retirement or global component-disposal change. The duplicate method summary was replaced with the source-window eligibility contract.

## Test Evidence

The red control failed through `onWindowPositionChange` before the guard existed. The same arm then passed with the existing live-source and re-entry controls. The first full CI unit run had one failure in the cancellation fixture (no source window registered); the unchanged assertions pass after its fixture declares that live source.

`WorkstationNativeTitlebarDragNL.spec.mjs`, “a popup moved by its OS titlebar previews the zone under its corner and reintegrates there under dwell”, passed **1/1 in 9.6s** using the explicit E2E config, `--headed --workers=1`, this checkout and its own web server. It preserves the ordinary physical popup-return path. This is a source-tree native-browser witness, not an installed Fleet update or a repaired packaged-candidate replay.

The earlier candidate's missing-parent messages remain unresolved and are not claimed fixed here.

### 🪜 Strategic-Fit Decision

Per §9 Strategic-Fit Step-Back:

- **Rationale**: One guard at the one call site, reading the registry that `Window.onWindowDisconnect` already maintains. It adds no second liveness cache and leaves Group/document retention alone. Nothing here needs a return cycle.

**Peer-Review Opening:** Thanks, Sophie. This is a clean bound on a real crash. The guard sits at the one site that iterates retained resolvers. It does not catch-and-discard, and it does not retire anything a Group still owns. The renewed-eligibility arm, re-registering the same window id, is the control I'd have asked for.

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** #19764 (the uncaught `NativeLifecycle.ownerEntries` stack, its design authority, and AC-1–AC-5) · `dev` `src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs#getNativeWindowDragSource` (`:590`) and its caller `onWindowPositionChange` (`:1228`) · `src/manager/Window.mjs`: `onWindowConnect` registers every window, the main one included (`:181`), `onWindowDisconnect` unregisters (`:218`), and a position event can register a geometry-only placeholder first (`:169`) · `src/worker/App.mjs:726–727`, which loads the Window manager under `useSharedWorkers`.
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** Skip a retained zone whose own window is no longer registered, read live at lookup time. Don't hardcode a second liveness flag or a tombstone, and don't wrap resolvers in try/catch. Isolation: a unit arm through the real disconnect handler with a live-source positive control.
*   **Patch Verdict:** Matches. `if (!Window.get(sortZone.windowId)) continue;` (`DragCoordinator.mjs:593`) is exactly that read. The arm disconnects through `WindowManager.onWindowDisconnect`, so it exercises the registry the guard reads, not a stub of it.
*   **Premise Coherence:** Coheres with verify-before-assert. The fix rests on an observed stack trace, the PR keeps the separate missing-parent observation explicitly unclaimed, and the packaged replay stays residual on #674.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge:** A zone whose `windowId` is unset now drops out of native lookup, because `Window.get(undefined)` is null. Before, it was invoked. I looked for a production zone that reaches native lookup without a window and found none. Native window drag only exists with shared workers, every component there carries its `windowId`, and in dedicated-worker mode there is no popup for the lookup to find. The edge is real but unreachable today. It is worth one clause in the method's JSDoc if a windowless participation ever appears.
